title: Self-driven ops kaizen notebook
content:
Purpose: scratchpad to collect short-term goals, evidence threads, and manager-facing talking points. Use this for 1:1 prep and to shape my upcoming self-review.

Right-now snapshot (feelings + facts):
- energy: medium-high, excited about cohort onboarding improvements but stretched on headcount asks.
- biggest friction: unclear ownership on the action items after OKR syncs; need tighter follow-ups.
- quick wins visible: reduced onboarding time for ICs by ~18% (pilot), churn in onboarding mentors down.
- hypothesis: structured mentor shadowing is the lever that explains onboarding delta; need A/B next quarter.

Concrete 90-day goals (measurable):
1) Mentor program pilot -> Ship repeatable process and metrics dashboard by end of Q2. Target: reduce average ramp time from 30d to 25d for pilot cohort.
2) Hiring playbook: complete draft for L4-L6 conversion interviews + scorecard for role fit. Target: 6 hires using the same rubric within 3 months.
3) Ops cadence: run weekly action review for OKR owners, reduce stale action items >2w from 42% to <15%.

12-month north star (signal):
- Establish a People Ops runbook that other teams copy for onboarding + role calibration. Revenue/cost tie: lower time-to-fully-productive -> lower support overhead for product onboarding flows.

Evidence bank (short snippets I can paste into review):
- Onboarding pilot: led cross-functional M&E with Eng + Product; built checklist + mentor rota; measured ramp via first-sprint task completion curve (see raw sheet link). Outcome: median first-month contribution improved.
- Interview rubric: consolidated hiring notes from 12 candidates into 4 shared scorecards; converted into a template we use in two interviews this cycle; hiring manager feedback: "more consistent, faster decisions".
- Cost/efficiency: renegotiated external training vendor terms -> saved ~$18k annually and expanded internal curriculum access.

Manager prep (1:1 talking points)
- Lead with the wins: onboarding pilot metrics + mentor engagement (brief headline and 1 line of underlying evidence).
- Ask: request headcount uplift (+1 L4 recruiter headcount) to maintain velocity on hiring playbook (rationale: throughput increases but recruiter capacity is saturated; show time-per-hire data).
- Ask: propose a 30-day experiment budget of $3k for A/B mentor formats (structured office hours vs paired shadowing).
- Risk to flag: retention risk in mentors — two high-engagement mentors have competing offers; mitigation plan ready (lite manager touchpoints, incremental recognition).
- Career/progression note: I want to discuss stretch scope into strategic sourcing and data instrumentation ownership for People Ops. Suggested success metric: own + deliver the recruitment dashboard by end of Q3.

Snippets for promotion/self-review narrative (copyable)
- "Led a cross-functional pilot that shortened ramp time for new ICs by 18% through a repeatable mentor program and playbook; documented process and created an onboarding dashboard for continuous measurement."
- "Standardized interview scorecards across interviews, improving decision consistency and reducing time-to-offer by X days (see JIRA-HR-1982)."

Quick wins / TODO (actionable, sorted)
- [ ] Finalize mentor rubric and send to Eng lead (Lina) for sign-off (due in 3 days).
- [ ] Share recruiter capacity analysis with manager before Tues 1:1.
- [ ] Draft experiment brief and budget line for A/B mentor formats.
- [ ] Pull first-month-sprint completion data and drop into one-pager.
- [ ] Archive pilot retrospective notes into Confluence under hr/onboarding/pilot-2026.

Open questions / hypotheses to test
- Does mentor shadowing reduce time-to-first-review more than scheduled office hours? Need to define metric (first-sprint task completion vs subjective readiness).
- How much recruiter time is consumed by sourcing vs coordination? Could automation of scheduling buyback 20% of time?

Potential blockers and remediation ideas
- Blocker: recruiting vendor SLA delays. Remediation: switch to second vendor pool and schedule weekly syncs to remove bottlenecks.
- Blocker: data latency in engagement metrics. Remediation: short-term manual pulls + longer-term request to instrumentation team for event-based tracking (linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE-hr/promo-criteria).

Meeting prep snippets (soundbites)
- "Quick update: pilot reduced ramp; looking to scale with a small experiment budget and one recruiter uplift. Can I get your support to prioritise headcount for hiring throughput?"
- If asked about risk: "Two mentors expressed interest in leaving; proposing small retention touches (spot recognition + manager check-ins) while we harden the program so it's less person-dependent."

Calendar & follow-ups
- Next 1:1 with manager: 2026-03-10 (prep: capacity analysis + one-pager on pilot outcomes).
- Team sync: weekly Thu 10am — bring action-item list.

Notes to self (raw, unpolished)
- Keep quotes for review: "consistency > perfection".
- Save small wins to the evidence bank weekly; helps during calibration conversations.
- When asking for HC, always lead with throughput data + cost of vacancy.

End-of-doc: quick reference links (copy into Confluence later)
- raw metrics sheet: SHEET-ONBOARD-2026 (internal)
- mentor feedback doc: DOC-MENTOR-FEEDBACK-MAR2026
- recruitment dashboard proto: DRAFT-RECRUIT-DASH

-- Asha
